annotations.text:
KAMPR — soft native, themeable.

Every artboard carries a Theme tweak: soft / phosphor / warm / brutalist. Nothing hardcodes a colour, font or radius. Soft native ships; the rest stay one attribute away.

KAMPR NEVER RESIZES A SESSION.

Earlier drafts borrowed the pane's shape to make it fit a phone. That is gone. Probed on 0.8.2: `terminal session control` ALWAYS claims geometry — there is no flag to decline it, and while it holds, the desktop client's own resize is ignored outright. So Kampr does not use control mode at all.

Instead: `observe` at the pane's native size (which never touches the PTY) for pixels, and the plain JSON API for keystrokes. Both are read-shaped as far as the session is concerned. The pane stays 94x40 for everyone, always.

Which makes the phone problem a rendering problem, where it belongs: pinch-zoom and pan over the real grid, zoom remembered per pane per device, and a Conversation view that sidesteps the grid entirely for agent panes.

Costs one thing, stated plainly: no `terminal.scroll`, so the live terminal shows the viewport only. Agent panes get their history from the transcript instead, which is better anyway.

CONVERSATION is the default for agent panes, and reflows natively — no zooming, no panning. It can answer a pending prompt without touching the terminal stream: question from the transcript, answer as keys.  ·  TERMINAL is the default for shell panes, zoomed to a readable size with a pan indicator under the grid.
ZOOM — presets, a minimap of where you are in the 94x40 grid, follow-cursor, and remembered per pane. The footer says the quiet part out loud: this is your view, not the session's shape.

SETUP starts from working, not from configuration.  ·  TYPING is drawn at 390x470 — the visible area with the on-screen keyboard up. The native OSK owns everything below that edge; the key row docks to it, and characters echo back from the pane as you type. No compose box, no Send button.

LANDSCAPE — 844 px fits the native 94 columns at 13 px with no zoom and no panning at all. This is why landscape is a first-class layout rather than a rotation fallback: it is the one phone orientation where a desktop-shaped pane simply fits.

DESKTOP — terminal and conversation side by side. Sidebar is the whole mesh grouped by node with real latencies. Status strip reads "no lease held — desktop shape untouched", which is now not a promise about behaviour but a statement of what Kampr structurally cannot do.
